text.p: Shares in the upcoming phase of a selloff in Hungarian drugs firm Richter Gedeon will be fully subscribed and the stock will certainly be sold at discount, analysts said on Wednesday.
"The only question now is that there are some other good quality alternatives in the region," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe in London.
"But I think Richter still is viewed among the first-rank regional good quality pharmaceuticals."
Monson said he saw a discount of two to four percent to the market price.
Hungary's state privatisation agency will sell 1.8 million Richter shares, while the company is issuing one million new shares.
Investors showed this week how positively they regard the stock.

Following the release of the company's first quarter earnings reports in the bourse's official gazette Richter's price rallied to a new record and on Wednesday it rose further to yet another record high of 14,250 forints.
Richter's roadshow will start next week and analysts said the offer might trigger speculation already seen in other shares approaching an IPO.

"Buying interest could decline just as it did in the case of MOL," said Gaspar Czako, analyst at Eastbrokers in Budapest, adding that traders expect the offer price to be at a discount compared with current prices.
